events.comment: CRACKLINE — Phase 3. Endless Depth and Planet Breaker share this one scene (GameMode global). Each system lives in its own external events sheet (Project manager > External events). Order matters.

GAME STATE — scene setup, best score loading, invulnerability timer, game over overlay and restart. GameState is "Playing" or "GameOver". GameMode (global) is "Endless" for now; Planet mode arrives in Phase 3 and will reuse this same scene.
Load the personal best saved on this device (GDevelop storage). NOTE: Playgama requires its Bridge storage instead; this gets swapped when the SDK is integrated.
Planet-mode HUD (surface progress bar) only in Planet Breaker; Endless shows only the Ember background.
Restart: tap/click the RESTART button. Restarting the scene resets every scene variable; global variables (best score, mode) persist.

SIMULATE AD REVIVE (TEST) button: it only REQUESTS a revive (RequestRevive = true); EV_Revive does the work. A future Playgama rewarded-ad 'rewarded' callback should set RequestRevive the same way. No ad is shown or faked here.
Impact flash fades out and grows.

PLANET BREAKER — same engine as Endless; this sheet only adds planet themes, the surface progress bar and the planet-splitting sequence. Planets cycle Ember -> Verdant -> Frost -> Ember...; each lap adds PlanetCycleExtraDistance and difficulty keeps rising (see EV_CrackMovement).
Runs once at scene start and after every broken planet: picks the theme, target distance and theme modifiers (Verdant = more crystals, Frost = more barriers/solid barriers).

parameters: "PLANET " + ToString(PlanetIndex + 1) + "  " + PlanetName + "   " + ToString(min(PlanetDistance, PlanetTargetDistance)) + " / " + ToString(PlanetTargetDistance) + " m"

events.name: Reach the surface -> break the planet

events.comment: Event-driven animation (BreakTime seconds): 0-0.35 planet pops in, 0.35-0.75 a glowing crack runs down its centre, 0.75-1.45 the two halves fly apart with an ease-out, then a message; at BreakDuration the next planet starts.
CRACK MOVEMENT — the crack tip stays at TipScreenY; the world scrolls instead. CrackWorldY = distance travelled upward in px.

Speed grows SpeedGrowth (8%) every SpeedGrowthInterval (20 s), smoothly, capped at MaxSpeed. DifficultyLevel goes 0 -> 1 over DifficultyRampTime and drives the obstacle generator. Slow Time multiplies the effective speed by SlowTimeFactor.
Planet Breaker: difficulty steps up per planet (PlanetDifficultyStep) and rises a little within each planet; speed keeps growing with RunTime across planets.
One tap = one branch. Taps during a branch or the short cooldown are ignored (no queueing). Left half = left, right half = right.
Lateral offset follows an ease-out curve over BranchDuration (computed from elapsed time, so frame-rate independent). Clamped so the crack can never leave the screen or get stuck.

parameters: clamp(BranchStartX + BranchDirection * BranchDistance * (1 - pow(1 - BranchTimer / BranchDuration, 2)), EdgeMargin, SceneWindowWidth() - EdgeMargin)
clamp(BranchStartX + BranchDirection * BranchDistance, EdgeMargin, SceneWindowWidth() - EdgeMargin)

events.comment: PROCEDURAL OBSTACLE ROWS with a guaranteed safe route. The screen is split into LaneCount (7) lanes. Every row keeps a 2-lane wide CORRIDOR free (SafeLane and SafeLane+1). The corridor drifts by at most one lane per row (on most rows), and on a drift row the lanes of both the old and new corridor stay free, so the corridor is continuous. A 2-lane gap is always wider than one branch (130 px), so a branch can always land inside it. This rule was validated offline by brute-force searching every tap timing over 60 random 5-minute runs at the real speeds (tools: gen_sim.py).

Row types: EMPTY (nothing), WALL (every lane outside the corridor gets a reinforced barrier, a share of them breakable), SCATTER (each lane outside the corridor gets an obstacle with probability Density). Density, row spacing and the share of crystals/solid barriers rise with DifficultyLevel; empty rows become rarer.
The corridor drifts left or right on most rows (it stays put only CorridorStayChance of the time), so the player must keep moving.
Lanes inside the corridor are skipped: (lane - min) * (lane - max) > 0 only outside it.
ObjType: 1 small rock, 2 medium rock, 3 crystal, 4 breakable barrier, 5 solid barrier.
Anti-camping: if this lane is where the crack is right now (and outside the corridor), block it with BlockerChance, so going straight is rarely safe.

Power-ups: uncommon (PowerupChance per row, then a PowerupCooldownTime cooldown). Placed in the middle of the safe corridor, halfway to the next row, so they are always reachable and never inside an obstacle.

POWER-UPS — Slow Time: EffectiveSpeed x SlowTimeFactor (0.6 = 40% slower) for SlowTimeDuration real seconds; distance still follows real progress. Crack Strength: StrengthMaxCharges charges, each breaks one rock or breakable barrier (see EV_Collisions); crystals and solid barriers can't be broken. Picking it up again refills to max.
Crack colour shows Strength: orange-red while charged.

FRACTURE TRAIL — visual only (never tested for collisions). A segment is laid every TrailStep px from the last trail point to the current (slightly jittered) tip position, then scrolls with the world.

COLLISIONS — only the small hidden CrackHitbox at the tip is tested. Order matters: first Crack Strength breaks Breakable obstacles (rocks, breakable barriers), then anything still touched kills, unless InvulnerabilityRemaining > 0 (used by the revive in Phase 3).
Endless: best distance. Planet Breaker: best planets broken. Both saved locally.

REVIVE (modular). Anything that sets RequestRevive = true while GameState is GameOver triggers it: today the SIMULATE AD REVIVE (TEST) button, later the Playgama rewarded-ad callback. One revive per run (ReviveUsed). Score, distance, speed, difficulty and planet progress are all kept.
Clear lethal obstacles around the crack so it can't die again immediately (the 2 s protection covers the rest).
Protective glow while invulnerable.
SCORING / HUD — distance comes from the logical world position (CrackWorldY), so Slow Time slows the counter exactly as much as real progress.
